keywords: how should a sweater fit a woman
how should a sweater fit men
answer: A sweater fits when the shoulder seams sit at your shoulder bones, the body skims your chest with 2–4 in of ease, the sleeves end at your wrist bone, the ribbed cuffs and hem hold their shape without gripping, and the hem lands at your hip so it covers your waistband when you lift your arms.
intro: Knitwear stretches, relaxes and sometimes shrinks, so a sweater that fits well on day one is slightly neater than you might expect. Check the seams and the length, then move: reach forward, lift both arms and sit down. If you are buying one as a holiday gift, the gift-sizing section below shows how to get the size right without asking.

checklist.good: The shoulder seam lands at the outer edge of your shoulder bone, or slightly below it on a relaxed or drop-shoulder style.
checklist.tooTight: The seam rides up onto the top of your shoulder and the knit pulls across your upper back when you reach forward.
checklist.tooLoose: On a fitted style, the seam hangs 2 in or more down your upper arm and the knit bunches in the armpit.

checklist.good: The knit skims your chest or bust with about 2–4 in of ease all round; you can pinch roughly 1–2 in of fabric at each side.
checklist.tooTight: The stitches stretch open, horizontal lines form across the chest and a shirt underneath shows through the pattern.
checklist.tooLoose: Fabric hangs in folds at the sides and the sweater looks a size bigger from the side than from the front.

checklist.good: With your arms relaxed, the cuff sits at your wrist bone, or ½ in past it on a chunky knit that will be pushed up.
checklist.tooTight: Too short: the cuff stops above the wrist bone and pulls further up your forearm when you reach forward.
checklist.tooLoose: Too long: the cuff covers the base of your thumb and the sleeve stacks in rolls above the wrist.

checklist.good: You can raise both arms over your head and the whole body lifts only an inch or two.
checklist.tooTight: The armhole cuts into your armpit and the hem jumps several inches when you lift your arms.
checklist.tooLoose: The armhole drops low enough to create batwing folds under the arm on a sweater that is meant to be fitted.

checklist.good: A crew neck sits flat at the base of your neck, a V-neck lies flat on your chest and a turtleneck folds over without choking.
checklist.tooTight: The neckband presses on your throat or pulls the front of the sweater up toward your chin.
checklist.tooLoose: The neckband gapes, ripples or slides off to one side.

checklist.good: The ribbed hem ends at your hip bone, about 2–3 in below your belt, and still covers the waistband when you lift your arms.
checklist.tooTight: Too short: skin or a shirt tail shows at the waist when you reach up, or the ribbing grips and rides up over your belly.
checklist.tooLoose: Too long: the hem reaches the middle of your seat and the ribbing slouches instead of hugging the hip, unless it's a tunic-length style.

variations.heading: Fit by sweater style
variations.intro: The shoulder, sleeve and hem checks apply to every sweater. What changes is how much ease the style is meant to have.

items.name: Fine-gauge knits (merino, cashmere, cotton)
items.text: Thin knits are designed to be worn close to the body and often layered under a jacket. Keep 2 in of ease or less across the chest, seams at the shoulder bone and sleeves that end at the wrist. If you'll wear it under a blazer, it must not add bulk at the armholes.

items.name: Chunky and cable knits
items.text: Thick knits need more room because the yarn itself takes up space. Allow 4–6 in of ease, accept a slightly dropped shoulder, and expect the sleeves to be pushed up. A chunky sweater that is fitted like a fine knit will feel stiff and ride up.

items.name: Oversized sweaters
items.text: An oversized fit is deliberate: dropped shoulders, a wide body and longer sleeves. The neckline should still sit properly and the sleeves shouldn't swallow your hands. If the brand's chart already describes the style as oversized, buy your usual size rather than sizing up.

items.name: Cardigans
items.text: A cardigan should button without the placket pulling into a zigzag between buttons, and should hang straight when open. Leave enough room to wear a shirt or tee underneath. Hip length is the most versatile; a longline cardigan should end mid-thigh.

items.name: Turtlenecks and mock necks
items.text: These are usually cut closer to the body. The collar should fold once, sit against your neck without pressing, and keep its height through the day. A loose turtleneck collar slumps by afternoon.

items.name: Women's and men's cuts
items.text: Women's sweaters usually have narrower shoulders, more shaping at the waist and shorter sleeves; men's are straighter through the body with longer sleeves. Either works on anyone, as long as the shoulder seam and sleeve length checks pass.

measure.heading: How to measure for a sweater
measure.intro: Measure over a thin T-shirt, standing relaxed, with a soft tape. Compare the numbers with the brand's size chart rather than the letter on the label.
steps: Chest: wrap the tape under your arms around the fullest part of your chest or bust, keeping it level across your back.
Shoulders: measure across your back from the outer edge of one shoulder bone to the other.
Sleeve: with your arm slightly bent, measure from the shoulder bone, over the elbow, to the wrist bone.
Length: measure from the base of your neck at the shoulder down to where you want the hem, usually your hip bone.
Compare: many brands publish garment measurements (the sweater laid flat). Double the pit-to-pit width to get the garment's chest and subtract your body chest to see how much ease you'll have.
measure.tip: Lay your best-fitting sweater flat and measure it from armpit to armpit and from shoulder seam to cuff. Those two numbers are the most reliable shortcut when a brand publishes garment measurements.

sizeTable.caption: Typical sweater letter sizes with US, UK and EU equivalents
sizeTable.note: These are common conventions, not a standard every brand follows. Women's UK sizes usually run 4 above US sizes and EU sizes about 30 above. Always check the chest measurement on the brand's own chart.

problems.problem: The sweater shrank in the wash
problems.fix: Wool and cashmere shrink with heat and agitation. Soak the sweater in lukewarm water with a little hair conditioner, gently stretch it back to shape and dry it flat. Next time, wash cold on a wool cycle or by hand and never tumble dry.

Push or fold chunky sleeves up to just below the elbow. On a fine knit, a tailor or knitwear specialist can shorten sleeves, though it costs more than altering a woven shirt. Buying a size that fits the shoulders and shortening the sleeves beats sizing down.

problems.problem: The hem flares or curls up
problems.fix: The ribbing has relaxed or the body is too tight over your hips. Steam the ribbing and let it dry flat. If it rides up over your stomach every time, the sweater is too short or too small in the body; go up a size.
Steam the neckband and pat it back into shape while it's damp. Avoid pulling sweaters on and off by the collar, and fold knits instead of hanging them, which stretches the shoulders and neck.

problems.problem: The shoulders have bumps from a hanger
problems.fix: Dampen the bumps, smooth them by hand and let the sweater dry flat. Store knits folded on a shelf or in a drawer.
Friction from a tight armhole or a bag strap causes pilling. Remove pills with a sweater comb or fabric shaver, and choose a fit with a little more room through the arms.

extra.heading: Buying a sweater as a gift: getting the size without asking
extra.body: Check a sweater, hoodie or sweatshirt they already wear often and like the fit of: the size label tells you the letter size, and the brand tells you whose chart it follows. If you can borrow it briefly, lay it flat and measure armpit to armpit, then compare that width with the garment measurements on the new brand's chart. If they live with someone you can ask, ask about their usual size in one brand and buy that brand. When torn between two sizes, choose the larger for a chunky or casual knit and the smaller for a fine, fitted knit, and include a gift receipt.

extra.heading: Will it shrink or stretch?
extra.body: Expect natural fibers to change a little. Wool and cashmere can shrink if washed warm or tumble dried, and cotton knits tend to stretch and bag at the elbows and hem over a day of wear. Synthetic blends hold their size best. Read the care label before you buy: a hand-wash-only sweater bought slightly too small won't grow, while a cotton knit that fits snugly will relax with wear.

extra.heading: Layering
extra.body: If you'll wear a collared shirt underneath, make sure the collar sits flat inside a crew neck or V-neck and the shirt cuff can show about ¼ in beyond the sweater cuff. To wear a sweater under a coat or blazer, choose a fine knit with a close fit through the arms; a chunky sweater belongs on the outside.

picks.label: Fine-gauge merino crew neck sweater
picks.why: A close, layerable fit that works under a jacket and is easy to size for a gift.

picks.label: Chunky cable knit sweater
picks.why: A relaxed fit is more forgiving when you're unsure of someone's exact size.

picks.label: Button-front cardigan
picks.why: Wears open or closed, so the fit across the chest matters less.

picks.label: Sweater comb or fabric shaver
picks.why: Removes pilling so a well-fitting sweater keeps looking new.

picks.label: Mesh laundry bag for knits
picks.why: Cuts friction and stretching in the wash, which protects the fit.

faqs.q: How should a sweater fit a woman?
faqs.a: The shoulder seams should sit at your shoulder bones, the knit should skim your bust without pulling or gaping between stitches, the sleeves should reach your wrist bone and the hem should land at your hip. Cropped and oversized styles change the length and ease on purpose; the shoulder and sleeve checks still apply.

faqs.q: How should a sweater fit a man?
faqs.a: Shoulder seams at the shoulder bones, about 2–4 in of ease around the chest, cuffs at the wrist bone and a hem that covers the belt by 2–3 in. A fine knit should be close enough to wear under a jacket; a chunky knit can be looser.

faqs.q: Should a sweater be tight or loose?
faqs.a: Neither. It should skim your body with a little ease, so you can pinch 1–2 in of fabric at each side. Fine knits sit closer and chunky knits sit looser, but no sweater should stretch the stitches open or hang in folds.

Buttoned, a cardigan should lie flat with no pulling between buttons, and open it should hang straight. The shoulder seams should meet your shoulder bones and the sleeves should end at your wrists, with room for a shirt or tee underneath.

faqs.q: Should I size up in sweaters?
faqs.a: Only if you want a relaxed look, plan to layer a thick shirt underneath, or the sweater is wool you'll wash at home and risk shrinking. If the brand already calls the style oversized, buy your usual size.

faqs.q: How do I find someone's sweater size for a gift?
faqs.a: Check the label of a sweater or hoodie they wear often, or measure one flat from armpit to armpit and compare it with the new brand's garment measurements. If you're between sizes, buy the larger in a casual or chunky knit and keep the gift receipt.

faqs.q: Where should the hem of a sweater sit?
faqs.a: At your hip bone, roughly 2–3 in below your belt, so it still covers your waistband when you raise your arms. Shorter cropped styles and longer tunic styles are exceptions by design.
